info.title: Skill Trees API
info.description: Backend API for a public skill-tree sharing site. Reading is public and needs no account; creating or changing a tree requires a session, and a tree may only be modified by the account that created it. Zero external dependencies: node:http and node:sqlite only. Errors are RFC 9457 problem details (application/problem+json) that keep the older `error` (and, for rejected imports, `problems`) members. Every GET also answers HEAD. A known path asked with a method it doesn't take answers 405 with an Allow header (components/responses/MethodNotAllowed), and OPTIONS answers Allow with no CORS headers: cross-origin use is unsupported. A request body must be declared application/json, or it is refused with 415. Cross-site requests are refused with 403 unless they are top-level GET navigations (W3C Fetch Metadata), as are state-changing requests whose Origin is another host. Responses are compressed (br, gzip) when the client accepts it, and GETs carry an ETag and answer If-None-Match with 304.

tags.name: Auth
tags.description: Accounts, sessions, and sign-in through GitHub, Google or an OpenID Connect provider

201.description: Account created; a session cookie is set

200.description: Signed in; a session cookie is set

post.summary: Sign out and invalidate the session
post.description: Deletes the session server-side and clears the cookie. Also sends Clear-Site-Data: "cookies", so the browser drops every cookie this site set — a leftover plain-named session cookie from before the __Host- rename, and the flow cookie of an unfinished provider sign-in.

200.description: Signed out; the session cookie is cleared
The current account, or null when signed out

get.summary: The providers "Continue with ..." is offered for
get.description: Every provider configured on this server (GitHub, Google, a generic OpenID Connect provider). Empty when none is. Only an id and a label: never a client id or secret.

post.summary: Begin signing in (or connecting an account) through a provider
post.description: Creates a single-use, ten-minute flow server-side (state, PKCE S256 verifier, OIDC nonce, the validated next path) and returns the provider's authorization URL, which the page then navigates to. Sets an HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax cookie binding the flow to this browser (__Host-skilltree_oauth over HTTPS, skilltree_oauth otherwise). A POST with a JSON body rather than a link or form so the same-origin check guards it (a GET start with intent=link would be CSRF-able) and so CSP form-action 'self' never meets a redirect off-site. intent=link requires a session and attaches the provider account to it. Throttled per address; a completed sign-in gives its count back.

200.description: Where to send the browser; the flow cookie is set

403.description: The request came from another site (Origin does not match)

503.description: The provider could not be reached (discovery failed), or too many sign-ins are unfinished

get.summary: Where the provider sends the browser back (the redirect_uri)
get.description: Not called by the page: the provider redirects here. The flow is looked up by state and deleted in the same step (single use), must carry this browser's flow cookie (login CSRF), must belong to this provider (mix-up), and must bring back iss equal to the provider's issuer when present — required when the provider advertises authorization_response_iss_parameter_supported (RFC 9207). The code is exchanged with the PKCE verifier and the same redirect_uri; an ID token is verified (signature against the JWKS, iss, aud/azp, exp/iat/nbf, nonce) or, for GitHub, the numeric user id is read from /user. Signs in to the account holding that (issuer, subject) — or a new one; never matched by email — or, for intent=link, connects it to the signed-in account. Always answers 303 and always clears the flow cookie.

parameters.name: error
parameters.description: Set by the provider when it did not issue a code; access_denied means the person declined.

303.description: Signed in or connected: to the flow's next path, with a fresh session cookie when signing in. Refused: to /account.html?oauth_error=<code>, where code is one of cancelled, expired, failed, unavailable, identity_taken, link_session — never text from the provider — plus &next= for a sign-in whose flow was found.

get.summary: The provider accounts connected to the signed-in account

delete.description: Refused with 409 when it is the last way to sign in: an account keeps at least one of a password or a connected provider that is configured now. Another account's identity answers 404, exactly like one that does not exist.

409.description: It is the only remaining way to sign in

200.description: Every tree, with its skill count

post.summary: Create a tree owned by the signed-in account

get.summary: One tree with its skills and prerequisite links

200.description: The tree, its skills and its links

patch.summary: Change a tree's title, description or author
patch.description: Only the account that owns the tree may do this. Trees created before accounts existed have no owner and are read-only for everyone.

delete.summary: Delete a tree and everything in it

post.summary: Add a skill to a tree

delete.summary: Delete a skill and its links

post.summary: Link one skill as a prerequisite of another
post.description: Both skills must belong to this tree, and the link must not create a cycle.

parameters.description: Override the tree's own layout mode.

200.description: The tree as a portable JSON document

Content-Disposition.description: Attachment filename derived from the tree title.

post.description: Dragging a skill is session-only and never saved, so the browser sends its current arrangement with the request when exporting as manual.

post.summary: Create a tree from a portable JSON document
Receive CSP violation reports from browsers
post.description: The endpoint pages name in Reporting-Endpoints (csp-endpoint) and in their CSP's report-to and report-uri. Takes the Reporting API's application/reports+json (an array of reports) and CSP2's application/csp-report (one report). Bodies are capped at 64 KB; the endpoint is throttled per address (10 per 15 minutes). Each report is logged as one line, with query strings removed from its URLs; nothing is stored.

SessionCookie.name: skilltree_session
SessionCookie.description: Opaque 256-bit session token. HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, Path=/. Over HTTPS the cookie is named __Host-skilltree_session, is Secure, and is the only name accepted there; skilltree_session is used over plain http (localhost) only.

SetSessionCookie.description: Sets or clears the session cookie.

SetFlowCookie.description: Sets (on start) or clears (on callback) the cookie binding a provider sign-in to this browser: HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, Path=/, ten minutes; __Host-skilltree_oauth and Secure over HTTPS. The callback also sets the session cookie when it signs someone in.

ETag.description: Strong validator for this representation (RFC 9110 §8.8.3), distinct per Content-Encoding. Send it back in If-None-Match to get a 304 when nothing changed.

Accept.description: The request media types this operation takes (RFC 9110 §15.5.16).

RetryAfter.description: Seconds to wait before trying again (RFC 9110 §10.2.3).

RateLimitPolicy.description: The quota policy that was hit, as an Internet-Draft structured field (draft-ietf-httpapi-ratelimit-headers-11): q is the quota, w the window in seconds. Advisory until the draft is published.

RateLimit.description: Remaining quota (r) and seconds until it is restored (t), per the same draft.

NotModified.description: The If-None-Match validator still matches; use the stored copy

BadRequest.description: The request was malformed or failed validation

Unauthorized.description: Not signed in, or the credentials were wrong

Forbidden.description: Signed in, but this is not your tree (or it has no owner and is read-only); or a cross-site request (Fetch Metadata, or an Origin that isn't this host)

MethodNotAllowed.description: The path exists but doesn't take this method. Not listed per operation, since it answers the methods that aren't there.

UnsupportedMediaType.description: The request body wasn't declared as a type this operation takes (application/json unless stated), wasn't UTF-8, or was content-encoded

ValidationProblems.description: The document was rejected, with a list of reasons

Error.description: An RFC 9457 problem details object. type is about:blank, so title is the HTTP status phrase; detail says what went wrong. error repeats detail for clients written before problem details.

ValidationError.description: A problem details object (see Error) that also lists each reason the document was rejected.

ReportList.description: A Reporting API upload (W3C Reporting API): a list of reports. Only type and body are read.

has_password.description: False for an account made through a provider, which has no password.

intent.description: login signs in (making an account for an identity never seen before, never matching by email). link connects the provider account to the signed-in account.

next.description: Where to go afterwards: a path on this site. Anything else — another origin, //host, /\host, a control character — falls back to /#browse (login) or /account.html (link).

authorization_url.description: The provider's authorization endpoint with response_type=code, client_id, redirect_uri (built from PUBLIC_ORIGIN), scope, state, code_challenge, code_challenge_method=S256 and, for OpenID Connect, nonce.

display_name.description: Which account at the provider this is, for display only (a GitHub login, a preferred username or email).

enabled.description: Whether it can sign in now: its provider is configured, under the same issuer.

LayoutMode.description: manual: stored coordinates are authoritative. auto: coordinates are ignored and the layout is computed from structure.

Timestamp.description: SQLite datetime('now') output in UTC: 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS'. Note this is not RFC 3339 (no 'T' separator, no offset).

featured.description: 1 for the homepage spotlight. Set server-side only; ignored if supplied in a request.

user_id.description: Owning account. null means the tree predates accounts and is read-only for everyone.

positions.description: Map of skill id to on-screen coordinates.

id.description: Slug, unique within the document. Skills reference each other by slug, never by database id.

requires.description: Slugs of the skills required before this one. All are required together.

Notation.description: The portable tree format described in FORMAT.md.
